messages:
Jess: FYI Lina at Acme opened a support ticket — they got a burst of residency compliance alerts after a planned failover. They say some requests appear in EU audit logs even though tenant has region=us-east.
Lina (customer-ops): They report p99 latency spikes and a few 403s. Pasted audit snippet showing policy=GDPR and served_region=eu-west-1 for tokens tied to acme-123.
Jess: Snippet from their ticket:
``
audit_event: residency_violation
tenant_id: acme-123
requested_region: us-east-1
served_region: eu-west-1
policy_trigger: true
timestamp: 2026-03-17T15:02:13Z
```
Tom (infra): @Jess can you share example request headers? need to inspect X-Client-Region and any geo headers / hints.
Jess: They included this curl repro:
``
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
     -H "X-Client-Region: us-east-1" \
     -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Jess: But audit shows those were served in eu-west-1.
RoutingBot: auto: failover executed for pool: gpt-serve-prod-1 due to capacity_pressure in us-east-1 at 2026-03-17T15:01:40Z. Fallback target: eu-west-1. Request headers preserved.
Matt (oncall): That matches our alarms — automated failover triggered by burst. Why did residency policy not block or mask? For strict residency we should DENY on cross-region fallback.
Priya (security): If fallback target is out-of-residency, enforcement should kick in before serving. We need to check the policy enforcement hook between router and serve plane.
Tom (infra): Pulling routing decision logs for tenant acme-123 now.
Tom (infra): Found decision trace:
``
decision_id: d-8791
reason: capacity_pressure
fallback_region: eu-west-1
policy_check: SKIPPED (cache-miss)
```
Jess: SKIPPED (cache-miss) — that's the smoking gun. Policy check missed on that decision.
Priya (security): Why did the policy_check cache miss? We cache residency rules per-tenant for 5s. If cache layer was overloaded it may return null and router defaulted to allow+failover.
Matt (oncall): I see SLO spike on policy service around 15:01 — CPU spike and a GC pause. Service returned 503 for some queries.
Tom (infra): Current routing behavior: when policy service unavailable we default to permissive mode with an audit event. That was intentional for availability but is unacceptable for tenants with residency.mode=strict.
Lina (customer-ops): Acme has residency.mode=strict in their org config. They expect DENY, not permissive audit.
Jess: They also attached billing notices — affected requests were billed under EU ingress pricing.
Priya (security): Priorities: 1) stop further cross-region serving for strict tenants 2) harden policy service (cache/circuit-breaker) 3) provide remediation and full audit export to customer.
Matt (oncall): Immediate mitigation: flip router behavior to enforce deny-on-policy-unavailable for tenants tagged residency.mode=strict. I can push a safe toggle.
Tom (infra): I'll prepare rollout: feature-flag change, canary 5% of routers, monitor 403/latency, then promote.
Jess: @Lina confirm customer wants immediate enforcement. They're asking for an immediate block on cross-region serving.
Lina (customer-ops): Yes — they requested immediate enforcement and a postmortem. They want list of affected request ids and timestamps.
Tom (infra): Rolling change command (canary):
``
./routerctl set-policy-fallback-mode --tenants-file=tenants/strict-residency.json --mode=deny --canary=0.05
```
RoutingBot: auto: config applied to 5% of router instances at 2026-03-17T15:10:02Z.
Tom (infra): Created INF-4521 to increase policy service cache, add circuit-breaker, and improve observability.
Priya (security): For the customer audit response: we'll provide the extracted audit lines and a signed statement of which requests were served in eu-west-1. @AuditorBot, export events for tenant acme-123 between 2026-03-17T15:00:00Z and 2026-03-17T15:05:00Z with event ids and request ids.
AuditorBot: auto: export queued. Generating audit bundle: tenant=acme-123 start=2026-03-17T15:00:00Z end=2026-03-17T15:05:00Z. ETA ~3min.
Jess: I'll draft the customer message: apology, root cause (transient policy service failure -> permissive fallback -> cross-region serve for strict tenant), immediate mitigation (enforced deny), data export, and planned fixes (policy resilience + router default change). Need approvers.
Priya (security): Approved. Add note: to our knowledge no PII was exfiltrated beyond normal request content; still treat as a compliance incident and escalate.
Matt (oncall): After canary looks good we'll roll to 100% for strict tenants; non-strict tenants stay permissive for availability.
Tom (infra): Canary metrics stable. If no regressions I'll promote to 100% at 15:20.
Jess: Customer asked whether tokens need rotation.
Priya (security): Token rotation not required — routing decision did not expose keys. Recommend rotation only if they prefer conservative posture.
Lina (customer-ops): I'll send the audit export and remediation note once 100% rollout confirmed. Created support ticket INC-2026-873.
Jess: Follow-ups: INF-4521 (policy service), DOCS-998 (update residency fallback docs), PMR assigned to Tom, notify compliance.
Tom (infra): Notifying compliance team now.
ComplianceBot: auto: incident logged INC-2026-873; severity=high; alerting compliance@redwood.
Matt (oncall): Monitoring. Will post final update after full flip.
Jess: Final: include list of affected request ids from audit bundle when AuditorBot finishes.
